marks.gloss_en: לא -- סבר כי היכי דלא לילפן גופא נוכראה: no, he held [they should be apart] so that they would not grow used to a foreign body (= p_taam_lo_yilfan_guf_nochri)
[Shmuel's father] held: [he kept them apart] so that they would not grow used to a foreign body
ועביד להו מקוה ביומי ניסן -- מסייע ליה לרב: his making a mikveh for them in Nisan supports Rav; he held, lest the dripping be more than the flowing
Rav: rain in the West -- its great witness is the Euphrates
Shmuel: the river is blessed [increases] from its own bed
Abaye: may a woman use artifice and fasten [her garment] on a nut in order to carry it out to her young son on Shabbat?
one may use artifice [to save garments] at a fire
there [at a fire, artifice is permitted] because if you do not permit him, he will come to extinguish
there [at a fire, artifice is forbidden because] that is the way of carrying out
R' Meir: the amputee goes out [on Shabbat] with his wooden leg
והאמרת רישא ״פורפת״ -- you said in the first clause 'she may fasten', yet the latter clause says she may not fasten ab initio on Shabbat (kind svara: no kind names a רישא/סיפא contradiction)
אמר אביי: סיפא אתאן למטבע -- the latter clause has come to the coin (= p_abaye_seifa_matbea)
Abaye: [in] the latter clause we have come to the coin -- the ab-initio prohibition is said of the coin
